PullRequest.Title: Unify worktree isolation across agents
PullRequest.Body: ```Copilot Generated Description:``` Extract worktree session isolation into a shared controller for Copilot, Codex, and Claude agents, ensuring consistent folder/worktree isolation. Refactor agent classes to utilize this shared controller and add unit tests for the new functionality. Update various components and styles to support the changes.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed send path unconditionally awaits the hook for every turn; the hook routes every non-pending file-backed session through resolveWorkingDirectoryForResume, whose first operation is fs.access. The call path and per-turn multiplicity are explicit; only the absolute latency varies with filesystem type.
Findings.PerformanceResource: one filesystem access operation for the session working directory on every user turn
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The added I/O grows linearly with the number of messages across all file-backed folder and already-materialized worktree sessions; one stat/access is performed before each send, including warm sessions.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased turn-start latency and reduced throughput, especially when the working directory is on a slow or network-mounted filesystem
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The send path changed model/agent selections and called agent.chats.sendMessage directly; working-directory existence repair was performed when resuming a session, not before each message.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every call to _sendTurnMessage now awaits resolveWorkingDirectoryBeforeSend. Once a session is no longer pending, AgentService calls resolveWorkingDirectoryForResume, which serializes per session and awaits fs.access even for an ordinary folder that is already active.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line 1430 unconditionally awaits resolveWorkingDirectoryBeforeSend before every agent send; AgentService's added non-pending branch calls resolveWorkingDirectoryForResume, and WorktreeIsolation._resolveWorkingDirectoryForResume immediately awaits fs.access(workingDirectory.fsPath).
Findings.Title: Resolve the working directory only during materialization
Findings.Impact: Each message waits for an unnecessary filesystem round trip before selection updates or the agent subprocess can receive the prompt. On remote/network-mounted repositories this can visibly delay every turn; locally it still adds repeated I/O across long chats.
Findings.Evidence: _sendTurnMessage is the common user-turn path. AgentService._resolveWorkingDirectoryBeforeSend only skips work for workspace-less sessions; for any file URI with pending=false it calls AgentConfigurationService.resolveWorkingDirectoryForResume -> WorktreeIsolation.resolveWorkingDirectoryForResume -> _resolveWorkingDirectoryForResume -> fs.access. Pending is cleared after first-send resolution, so all subsequent turns still take this boundary.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep repair in the actual resume/materialization path, or cache/mark the resolved directory after the first send and return it directly for live sessions. The common warm-turn path should not call resolveWorkingDirectoryForResume or fs.access.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The before/after scheduling is explicit in the diff: config resolution moved from a Promise.all after provider creation to an await before provider creation, and customization retrieval is now awaited afterward. The shared resolver's sequential git commands and customization providers' disk-backed work establish expensive boundaries; exact duration varies by repository and customization count.
Findings.PerformanceResource: git subprocesses plus provider/session initialization and customization filesystem scans
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The added serial latency is paid once per createSession with a working directory; git probe cost depends on repository/filesystem latency and customization cost grows with configured/session customization files.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: longer new-session creation latency before the client receives the created session
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Provider creation and side-effect initialization ran first in parallel, then _resolveCreatedSessionConfig and getSessionCustomizations ran together in a Promise.all, allowing git-backed config resolution and customization discovery to overlap.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The code now awaits _resolveCreatedSessionConfig before starting provider.createSession, waits for provider creation, and only then starts/awaits getSessionCustomizations, turning the three setup stages into a serial chain.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 928 awaits _resolveCreatedSessionConfig before the Promise.all that starts _createProviderSession; added lines 976-981 await getSessionCustomizations only after that Promise.all. The deleted hunk ran config resolution and customization retrieval in one Promise.all after provider creation.
Findings.Title: Keep session setup work overlapped
Findings.Impact: Creating any repository-backed session can now wait for the full git config probe, provider setup, and customization discovery in sequence. Slow repositories or substantial customization trees make the delay visible before the new chat is ready.
Findings.Evidence: _withIsolationSchema calls WorktreeIsolation.resolveIsolationConfig, whose _getGitInfo performs getRepositoryRoot followed by revParse, getCurrentBranch, and getDefaultBranch; AgentHostGitService implements these as git subprocess calls (repository-root may be cached, the other probes are not). Copilot and Claude customization resolution can perform plugin/directory discovery, while Claude/Copilot provider creation itself also performs git/project and customization setup. All are on createSession's awaited critical path after the change.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the pending-worktree safety without serializing unrelated setup: derive/mark pending from the already-resolved isolation input when possible, keep provider creation concurrent for explicit folder sessions, and start customization retrieval as soon as the provider session exists while overlapping any remaining config/initialization work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a new folder- or worktree-backed Copilot, Codex, or Claude session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: createSession now awaits shared isolation/config resolution, then provider creation, then initial customization discovery before returning the created session. All three stages are on the client-visible critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve repository root, HEAD, current branch, and default branch through git
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to four sequential git calls per config resolution; repository-root lookup may be served from AgentHostGitService's in-memory cache, leaving three uncached probes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Copilot performed equivalent config probes later and overlapped config resolution with customization retrieval; Claude/Codex did not receive the shared host isolation probe.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Now completes before provider.createSession can begin.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One discovery snapshot per created session; scan size depends on configured and workspace customizations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Customization retrieval and created-session config resolution ran concurrently after provider creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Now begins only after config resolution and provider creation complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve project/git context during provider creation where supported
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Typically repository-root/worktree-list git calls once per session; repository-root may be cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider creation began immediately in parallel with side-effect initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider creation is awaited and now starts after shared config resolution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One execution per new session; cost grows with git/repository latency and the number/size of session customization files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within one session these stages changed from partial overlap to serialization. The git probes inside resolveIsolationConfig are sequential. Independent session creations can overlap, subject to git service sequencing and provider limits.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: getRepositoryRoot can be warm-cached by working-directory URI, but revParse/current/default branch probes are repeated. Provider customization controllers may reuse settled state when warm; cold directory discovery still occurs after provider creation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff explicitly moves config resolution before provider creation and removes the Promise.all that overlapped config and customization work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Absolute delay depends on git process startup, filesystem placement, and customization tree size; the serialization and boundary ordering are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable missing-coalescing regression because expensive setup phases that previously overlapped now execute serially.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send the first message in a fresh worktree-isolated session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before the provider can materialize and receive the prompt, the host resolves a branch name, creates the git worktree, optionally copies included files, persists metadata, and emits the announcement. This setup is intentionally on first-send's critical path so the subprocess cwd is correct.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Generate a branch-name hint through the Copilot utility API when authenticated
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one utility request per fresh worktree session; local prompt-derived fallback on failure/no token.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This existed for Copilot worktree sessions; Codex and Claude had no worktree first-send path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks branch selection and therefore worktree creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check branch collisions and run git worktree add
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one branch-existence check plus one worktree-add sequence; more checks only on name collision.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Equivalent work existed only in Copilot; Codex and Claude used the picked folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before provider materialization locks its cwd.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check candidate path, create worktree root, copy configured include files, and persist worktree metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One mkdir and metadata batch per worktree, plus bounded-concurrency copies for every matched include path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Equivalent work existed only for Copilot worktree sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All are awaited before the first agent send, except downstream logging.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Materialize provider SDK/app-server session in the resolved cwd
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider materialization per fresh provisional session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider materialization was already first-send work; Codex prewarm could begin earlier for folder sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Begins after worktree setup and then gates the first model turn.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One worktree creation per fresh session; collision checks scale with candidate collisions up to 100, and include-file copying scales with matched files/directories.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Lifecycle work is serialized per session, and branch/worktree creation is additionally serialized per repository. Different repositories can proceed concurrently. Include-file copies use the git service's existing limiter of 15.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Pending and created-worktree maps coalesce repeated/concurrent first sends; repository-root lookup is cached. Failed creation clears pending and falls back to the picked folder; no negative cache is needed afterward.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: pending markers and both sequencers explicitly bound multiplicity and ordering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Worktree checkout and include-copy duration vary greatly by repository and file set, but this is required feature work and is coalesced to once per session.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the new first-send cost implements requested isolation, is coalesced, and preserves the required cwd ordering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send subsequent messages in a live folder or already-materialized worktree session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every turn now awaits host working-directory resolution before model/agent selection updates and agent.chats.sendMessage. For a file URI, the non-pending path serializes and executes fs.access.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check that the effective working directory exists
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one fs.access on every normal turn while the directory exists; missing paths add database reads and git repair calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Warm sends did not validate the working directory; repair was associated with session resume.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks every prompt before it reaches the provider.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One access check per user message across every file-backed live session; aggregate cost grows linearly with chat turns.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Checks are serialized per session by WorktreeIsolation's sequencer; different sessions can probe concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no warm resolved-directory fast path. Pending is cleared after first send, but every later turn still calls resume repair and fs.access; only workspace-less sessions skip it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the unconditional send hook and transitive fs.access are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Local stat latency is usually small, while network-mounted or contended filesystems can make it visibly slow; multiplicity and critical-path placement are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-I/O regression on the warm turn path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore or list persisted sessions and reconstruct chat history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session listing awaits provider catalogs and one batched metadata read per session. Direct metadata restore additionally overlays the worktree project; default-chat history retrieval reads worktree metadata to restore the announcement. Provider resume validates or repairs the persisted cwd before SDK startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read session flags, git state, changeset metadata, and worktree repository root
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing batched metadata-object read per listed session; the diff adds one key, not another read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-session batch existed without the worktree repository-root key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks completion of the session catalog as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read branch/path/repository worktree metadata for project or announcement overlays
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One database open with three concurrent key reads per direct metadata/history overlay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Copilot history performed a similar worktree metadata read; Claude/Codex did not.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks direct restored metadata or default-chat history completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate persisted cwd and, when missing, read metadata and recreate/fallback
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One access check per actual provider resume; missing live worktrees add branch check plus worktree-add, archived ones add a repository-root access check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Equivalent repair existed inside Copilot only; Claude/Codex had no shared repair path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before provider SDK startup can read history safely.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Listing scales with provider session count but retains one metadata-object read per session; direct restore/history work occurs once per opened session/chat.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider catalogs and per-session list overlays use Promise.all. Worktree repair is sequenced per session. Metadata key reads within a worktree metadata lookup run concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: List overlay batches the new repository-root key into an existing DB read. Direct project and announcement lookups do not add explicit caches, but are bounded to metadata/history requests; existing directories take the fs.access fast path during resume.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for boundary counts and batching.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Database implementation/cache state and provider catalog sizes vary; no new collection-wide extra database pass was introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: list work remains batched, while added restore reads are bounded and support the new cross-provider worktree behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Archive, unarchive, dispose, or shut down worktree sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Archive/unarchive launch cleanup/recreation asynchronously after persisting the flag, so git work is off the archive action's critical path. Explicit dispose awaits provider teardown then per-session worktree removal. Shutdown awaits all providers, then removes all process-created worktrees.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read persisted worktree metadata and archived flags
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One DB open and a three-key metadata batch for each archive/unarchive lifecycle action that reaches the controller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Copilot performed equivalent work in provider-owned handlers; Codex/Claude did not manage worktrees.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the archive/unarchive protocol action critical path because AgentSideEffects does not await it; on resume it is awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check worktree/repository paths and create parent directories
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One or two checks per lifecycle operation, plus mkdir when recreating.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Equivalent lifecycle checks existed for Copilot only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background for archive/unarchive, awaited for explicit dispose/resume/shutdown as applicable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check branch and dirty state, remove or recreate git worktrees
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Archive of an existing clean worktree runs branch check, status, and remove; unarchive runs branch check and add; shutdown launches one remove per process-created worktree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Copilot owned equivalent per-session cleanup; shared ownership extends it to new providers and centralizes shutdown cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off archive/unarchive action progress; awaited during dispose/shutdown.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Per archive/unarchive operation, one session is inspected. Shutdown/removal scales with the number of worktrees created in the current host process.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A per-session sequencer prevents lifecycle races. Archive cleanup performs metadata, access, branch, dirty-state, and removal operations sequentially. Shutdown removal uses Promise.all across session keys, while each key remains individually sequenced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: In-memory created-worktree ownership avoids metadata lookup for dispose/shutdown removal. Archive/unarchive intentionally reads persisted metadata because sessions can outlive the current process. Removed entries are deleted from the map.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for lifecycle ownership, operation count, and sequencing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously process-created worktrees at shutdown is user-dependent. No evidence establishes a user-visible regression from the concurrent shutdown drain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: cleanup ownership is preserved, per-session races are serialized, and archive work is off the interaction critical path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 29 changed files and all diff pages. Reported two high-confidence regressions: per-turn filesystem validation on warm sends and serialization of session config, provider creation, and customization setup. First-send worktree creation, restore/list overlays, and lifecycle cleanup were traced through network, git subprocess, filesystem, and database boundaries; their remaining costs are bounded, batched, required by the feature, or off the relevant critical path.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
